# Fixed native lifecycle control source

This entrypoint is source-only and has not been compiled or executed. It invokes no Dafny product, creates no ProductContext, and never calls RunVerification. The four existing argument controls remain separate. Proof CLI mode is still unavailable. Lifecycle controls are infrastructure prerequisites, not verification or resource-cost parity evidence.

The only new syntax is `--lifecycle-controls --solver PATH --solver-sha256 HASH --cgroup-parent DIR --receipt PATH`. It requires Linux x64, a pinned native Z3 5.1.0 image and a trusted caller-created private, empty delegated cgroup-v2 parent with `pids.max=300`. The supported public CI setup invokes only this fixed harness through sudo with an already resolved absolute dotnet executable and records/asserts actual Linux effective UID0. This is an explicit privileged CI prerequisite, not an unprivileged deployment claim: non-root migration from a runner cgroup to a fresh delegated child also needs common-ancestor cgroup.procs write permission. The coordinator stays outside the private parent and does not chown or reconfigure any shared ancestor. It must not preserve GH_TOKEN or other coordinator credentials in the elevated environment. The caller must retain its own outer deadline and cgroup teardown authority. The harness never creates delegation or changes the caller's configuration. It runs exactly the eleven ordered names in `lifecycle-control-fixtures.json`; an unexpected outcome stops subsequent controls.

The caller compiles `native-lifecycle-fixture.c` only in public scratch CI, using the full nine-element command `[compilerAbs, -std=c11, -O2, -Wall, -Wextra, -Werror, sourceRelative, -o, binaryRelative]`. Publish `native-lifecycle-fixture` and `native-lifecycle-fixture.build.json` adjacent to the harness. The build receipt schema is version1 with `compiler{path,sha256,version}`, that exact `arguments` array, `sourceSha256`, `binarySha256` and `sourceManifestSha256`. The harness compares actual compiler/source/binary bytes and the source-manifest digest with those declarations. This receipt is a trusted CI declaration of its actions, not signed compiler-origin evidence. The native fixture has only fixed modes and at most257 forks; no shell or arbitrary executable mode exists. Its seal-check mode executes the fixed source-pinned Python component probe, which imports the reviewed wrapper's capture/write helpers without invoking its main routine or executing Z3.

The fixed controls exercise missing explicit private delegation (the cgroup root is deliberately passed and must produce the exact delegation rejection) and wrong pin (the exact digest rejection) before any product load; real sealed Z3 version/complete unchanged stream receipts; actual EPERM on write/grow/shrink/new-seal attempts plus source-copy mutation after sealed capture; a wrapper started by a dedicated .NET thread that retires while the host and Z3 stay alive (echo/exit only); exact binary input/output and independent fragmented stderr plus EOF; actual stdin relay EPIPE with unchanged stdout/stderr; a controlled timeout with a physically observed reparented session-leader descendant;257 live fixture descendants over the supervisor cap, requiring fault/fallback and empty removed cgroup; a launch refused after admission closure/removal, with a separate pre/post start-time verified direct-child pidfd guard in finally (any forced drain keeps the control failed); and a deliberately corrupted completion token following a successful fixture version prerequisite.

The partial-write component uses the exact production helper with a deterministic writer that returns bounded partial counts and raises one InterruptedError. This is an executed algorithm component control, not a claim about kernel pipe scheduling. The separate whole-wrapper control forwards native fragmented I/O and reports measured kernel partial counts, which can be zero. Wrapper counters cover completed forwarding blocks; a failed block is covered by its exact read/write hashes and error receipt, not advertised as a complete syscall count.

Each primitive scope is single-use. The orchestration may continue to a separate primitive negative test after an expected rejection has been proven, but it never creates or resumes a product verification context. It does not bypass Runs' poisoned-host rule. Negative tests pass only if the specific deliberate fault is observed, the supervisor rejects success, and the owned leaf is authoritatively empty and removed; fallback never turns a verification failure into verification success. Cap failure also requires the exact256-member fault and recorded owned-cgroup.kill request. The cap control waits at most five seconds for an immutable observation published by the real supervisor when its own cgroup membership read exceeds256; it records the observed count and exact fault code/message before cleanup. A fixture-side member count or a generic monitor-lock timeout cannot substitute for that observation. Cleanup must independently bind the same cap fact in its receipt. Malformed-completion rejection is exercised after an original zero-exit/token-valid receipt; arbitrary fixture failure cannot satisfy that control. Logs are bounded, streams read concurrently, input/exit/output waits are capped, and cleanup is always attempted on control failure.

`lifecycle.json` binds the source manifest, harness binary, solver, fixture source/binary/build receipt and individual cleanup/data hashes. It includes exact names/order, expected outcome, observed rejection/fallback, empty-owned facts and a fixed failure code; public CI declaration fields retain only public runner paths. Raw private per-scope evidence lives below the receipt directory and remains available for audit. After host termination and owned-cgroup cleanup, the coordinator may transfer ownership of only the newly created lifecycle evidence subtree for its public artifact uploader; it must not change ownership of unrelated files or shared cgroups. Missing receipts, unexpected exceptions, unfinished host children or retained owned groups fail the gate. Source-only parser/hash checks establish no runtime result.

Still required separately: the caller's independent host-death teardown control; pinned Z3 origin-resource/$ORIGIN inspection beyond a version invocation; actual successful native proof batches followed by weak-reference context collection; full query/result/RU denominators. None of these is claimed by lifecycle mode.
